brief: How to build an audience without posting every day

slots.title: Choose a rhythm you can hold in a bad week
slots.body: Daily is the advice everyone gives and almost nobody survives. Twice a week for a year beats daily for a month, every time.

slots.title: Write one thing worth quoting
slots.body: A single line people repeat does more than twenty posts nobody finishes. Aim for the sentence someone screenshots.

slots.title: Say the same thing in a new shape
slots.body: Your best idea deserves more than one airing. Most of your audience missed it the first time, and the second framing usually lands harder.

slots.title: Answer everyone for the first year
slots.body: Replies are where an audience actually forms. The algorithm rewards it, but more importantly the people remember it.

slots.title: Be narrow long enough to be known for it
slots.body: Breadth feels safe and reads as noise. People follow you for a specific thing, and they leave when that thing goes missing.

slots.title: Judge the year, never the post
slots.body: Single posts are noise. The only honest measurement window is long enough that luck averages out, and that window is months.

slots.headline: Pick one and hold it
slots.body: Not all six. The one you can still do in a week where everything else goes wrong is the one that will actually compound.
